one_liner: Closed-source Rust image-diff engine for Node (CIEDE2000, AA suppression, SSIM/GMSD); no current benchmark against odiff or pixelmatch.
what_it_does: A visual-regression image comparator shipped as the npm package @vizzly-testing/honeydiff, whose engine is a Rust native addon built with Neon. compare(baseline, current, options, artifacts) takes file paths or Buffers and returns JSON-only data: pixel counts split into rendered-equal, below-threshold, anti-aliasing, small-region, visual and structural populations, exact 8-connected diff regions with Delta E statistics, and height-change data; analyze() adds SSIM, MS-SSIM and GMSD, and separate calls do WCAG contrast screening and colour-vision-deficiency simulation. It is not a drop-in for odiff or pixelmatch: the threshold is in CIEDE2000 Delta E units (default 2) and the result shape is its own.
how_it_is_fast: The engine source is not public, so this comes from the CHANGELOG and symbol names in the shipped Linux x64 binary: rows are scanned in parallel on a rayon pool (compare_work collects per-row ScanSummary/RowDeltas), pixels with identical RGB skip the Lab conversion, and exact/no-AA count-only comparisons scan raw RGB rows directly (0.11.1). CIEDE2000 is computed in f64 through an sRGB-to-linear lookup table, regions are labelled with a union-find over row spans, SSIM uses a separable Gaussian blur in f64 with a direct path for small images, GMSD runs on 2x-downsampled luma, and height shifts are matched by row checksums. The x86-64 binary has no AVX instructions in its honeydiff_core functions (SSE2 only), so the speed comes from threads and short-circuits, not wide SIMD.
when_to_use: Node.js 22+ visual-regression pipelines (browser or app screenshots) that need a perceptual CIEDE2000 tolerance and anti-aliasing suppression rather than a raw pixel count.
Diff triage tooling that wants region bounds, Delta E statistics, SSIM/MS-SSIM/GMSD and diff fingerprints from one call, for example to group the same header change across many pages.
Full-page screenshots whose height changed by one inserted or removed block (alignHeightChanges: true keeps later changes visible).

Strict gates on very tall screenshots with threshold 0, antialiasing false and minimumRegionPixels 1: the author reports ~4.34 ms core time for an 18.3 MP (750x24,412) fixture versus ~147 ms in default mode.
Teams that also want WCAG contrast screening and CVD simulation from the same native package.
when_not_to_use: When end-to-end speed is the goal: the author's own README of 2026-05-19 (v0.10.3) measured odiff 4.2.1 at ~0.41 s against Honeydiff default ~1.27 s and exact/no-AA ~0.42 s on the tall fixture, so odiff was about 3.1x faster than the default mode (derived from page data).

When you need the engine source, a Rust crate, a C/C++ or Python API, or to build it yourself: the engine lives in a private repo (package.json points to vizzly-testing/r-honeydiff, 404), nothing is on crates.io or PyPI, and the MIT licence covers only the JS loader you can see.
On Intel macOS, musl/Alpine Linux or Node older than 22: prebuilt binaries exist only for macOS ARM64, Linux glibc x64/ARM64 and Windows x64, and the loader throws on anything else.

Where API stability matters: pre-1.0 with breaking changes in 0.4.0 (ESM only), 0.5.0 (YIQ options replaced by CIEDE2000), 0.11.0 (SSIM/MS-SSIM/GMSD values changed) and 0.16.0 (include flags and result fields removed).

Content with large anti-aliased or gradient areas in default mode: the AA path is ~34x the exact path on the tall fixture (147 vs 4.34 ms), and CHANGELOG 0.11.1 says synthetic full-surface gradient stress cases got slower after the stricter AA checks.

integration.form: shared lib (npm package with prebuilt Node native addons built with Neon 1.1.1; no Rust crate, C API or source)
integration.dependencies: none at runtime (package.json has no dependencies); the binaries statically include image 0.25.10 with default features (png 0.18.1, zune-jpeg, image-webp, tiff, exr, gif, rav1e/ravif), rayon 1.12 and neon 1.1.1
integration.min_toolchain: Node.js 22+ (engines >=22.0.0, ESM-only since 0.4.0); binaries report rustc 1.98.1; cannot be built from the public repo
integration.platforms: macOS ARM64, Linux x64 and ARM64 (glibc builds only), Windows x64; no Intel macOS or musl binaries
integration.thread_safety: Async APIs run as Neon tasks; all work shares one process-wide rayon pool sized by HONEYDIFF_THREADS or configureThreads(), which throws if the size is changed after work starts; concurrent-call guarantees otherwise not documented

gotchas: Withdrawn odiff claim: until 2026-05-19 the README said '6x faster than odiff (79ms vs 474ms)' on a 750x24,162 screenshot (Apple M-series). Commit 4021bb5 removed it, stated that the Honeydiff table is core time on preloaded images without PNG decode, process startup or file output, and reported end-to-end CLI runs on the tall fixture where odiff 4.2.1 (~0.41 s) beat Honeydiff default (~1.27 s) and matched exact/no-AA (~0.42 s). The 6x figure therefore appears to have set Honeydiff core time against an end-to-end odiff run; do not cite it.

No harness, hardware or fixtures are published (benchmarks/BENCHMARK_RESULTS.md and docs/REFERENCES.md return 404) and the README table changes every release: after the 0.11 metric-correctness change Full HD default went from ~18.9 to ~31.6 ms and 4K from ~77.7 to ~131 ms (v0.10.3 vs v0.11.1 READMEs), and by v0.15.0 those synthetic rows were replaced with the Vizzly and tall-screenshot fixtures. Core time excludes PNG decode, which dominates real runs (tall fixture exact: ~4.9 ms core vs ~0.42 s CLI).

The suppression logic has had false-negative bugs, the dangerous kind for regression tests: AA detection hid flat full-surface colour regressions (fixed 0.11.0) and thin border or divider recolouring (fixed 0.12.0), capped early-exit comparisons could report false identity (fixed 0.12.0, early exit removed in 0.16.0), and the 0.8.1 SSIM skip returned 1.0 when only AA-filtered pixels differed. The 0.8.1 '5x faster SSIM' (239 to 51 ms at 1920x1080) used integral images, i.e. a box window, before 0.11.0 switched to the Gaussian-weighted SSIM of the paper. Pin versions and re-baseline after upgrades.

Packaging: the 0.17.0 tarball is 14.7 MB (36 MB unpacked) with all four platform binaries; the Linux x64 .node is unstripped with debug info (10.3 MB) and carries an AVIF encoder (rav1e) and EXR/TIFF/GIF codecs from the image crate's default features; the x86-64 build uses SSE2 only.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over odiff when you need Delta E thresholds, anti-aliasing suppression, region statistics or SSIM/GMSD inside Node and can accept a closed engine; pick odiff (open source, with a published hyperfine comparison against ImageMagick and pixelmatch) when raw end-to-end speed or a standalone CLI matters, since Honeydiff's own README measured odiff about 3x faster than its default mode. imgdiff is obsolete.
verified_claims_summary: There is no current cross-library measurement: the README lists only Honeydiff's own core timings (Vizzly screenshot ~2.81 ms default and ~2.18 ms strict, 18.3 MP tall screenshot ~147 ms default and ~4.34 ms strict, 1080p SSIM ~14.7 ms, GMSD ~10.9 ms) with no hardware stated, though CHANGELOG 0.11.1 names local Criterion runs on Apple Silicon. The only head-to-head the author published (README of 2026-05-19, v0.10.3, end-to-end CLI on the tall fixture) has odiff 4.2.1 at ~0.41 s against Honeydiff's ~1.27 s default and ~0.42 s exact mode.
status_note: Actively released (0.17.0 on 2026-09-06, single maintainer, release-tag commits only) but reference-only: the public repo is a JS loader plus binaries, the Rust engine is private, and the author's own May 2026 end-to-end run shows odiff faster, so the earlier '6x faster than odiff' README claim should be treated as withdrawn.
